title: Microsoft Purview: auto-labeling ceiling for SharePoint and OneDrive rises to 500,000 files a day (Worldwide)
summary: The briefing's rollout, licensing and administrative controls are supported by the supplied records and Microsoft documentation. Two minor omissions remain: the governance checklist mentions policy conditions and label-encryption settings that have no corresponding controls-table entries.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; rationale: risk
claims.claim: SharePoint and OneDrive auto-labeling capacity increases from 100,000 to up to 500,000 files per tenant per day.
claims.quote: We are increasing the maximum auto-labeling capacity for SharePoint and OneDrive from 100,000 up to 500,000 files per tenant per day.

claims.claim: Auto-labeling policies are the service-side method for applying sensitivity labels to stored SharePoint and OneDrive files matching administrator-defined conditions.
claims.quote: Service-side labeling when content is already saved (in SharePoint or OneDrive) or emailed (processed by Exchange Online): Use an auto-labeling policy.

claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Scope; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: The increase automatically applies to existing active SharePoint and OneDrive auto-labeling policies.
claims.quote: The increased processing limit will automatically apply to existing active auto-labeling policies.

claims.claim: The capacity increase does not change policy configuration.
claims.quote: Policy configuration, labeling conditions, and label settings will not change.

claims.claim: The capacity increase does not change labeling conditions.
claims.quote: Policy configuration, labeling conditions, and label settings will not change.

claims.claim: The capacity increase does not change label settings.
claims.quote: Policy configuration, labeling conditions, and label settings will not change.

claims.claim: The notice gives a public preview rollout from early to late September 2026.
claims.quote: Public Preview: Rollout begins in early September 2026 and is expected to complete by late September 2026.

claims.claim: The notice gives a Worldwide General Availability rollout from early to late October 2026.
claims.quote: General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout begins in early October 2026 and is expected to complete by late October 2026.

claims.claim: The notice sets no act-by date.
claims.quote: Act by: none

claims.claim: Microsoft says no action is required for organisations already using auto-labeling policies.
claims.quote: No action is required for organizations currently using auto-labeling policies.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Microsoft expects no end-user experience changes.
claims.quote: No end-user experience changes are expected.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends that organisations not using auto-labeling create a SharePoint or OneDrive policy in simulation mode.
claims.quote: If you are not currently using auto-labeling, we recommend: Create an auto-labeling policy for SharePoint or OneDrive in simulation mode.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends reviewing simulation results before enabling the policy.
claims.quote: Review simulation results to validate expected labeling outcomes.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends enabling the policy after validation.
claims.quote: Enable the policy after validation to take advantage of the increased daily processing limit.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn describes 500,000 automatically labeled files per tenant per day as absolute maximum throughput.
claims.quote: The absolute maximum throughput is 500,000 automatically labeled SharePoint and OneDrive files per tenant per day

claims.claim: The 500,000-file ceiling is aggregated across all tenant auto-labeling policies.
claims.quote: in aggregate across all auto-labeling policies.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: The ceiling is not a guaranteed or consistently expected daily processing rate.
claims.quote: This ceiling isn't a guaranteed or consistently expected daily processing rate

claims.claim: Actual throughput can be lower than the ceiling.
claims.quote: actual throughput can be lower.

claims.claim: Roadmap item 571309 describes the same SharePoint and OneDrive auto-labeling capacity increase.
claims.quote: "id": 571309; "description": "We are increasing the maximum auto-labeling capacity for SharePoint and OneDrive from 100,000 up to 500,000 files per tenant per day.

claims.claim: Item 571309 lists GCC, GCC High and DoD separately.
claims.quote: "id": 571309; "clouds": ["GCC", "GCC High", "DoD"]

claims.claim: Item 571309 has status Launched.

claims.quote: "id": 571309; "targetDate": "November CY2026"

claims.claim: Learn says auto-labeling policies run continuously until deleted.
claims.quote: Auto-labeling policies run continuously until they're deleted.

claims.claim: New and modified files are included using the current policy settings.
claims.quote: For example, new and modified files will be included with the current policy settings.

claims.claim: The roadmap frames the change as closing labeling gaps and helping prepare data for Microsoft 365 Copilot.
claims.quote: closing labeling gaps across existing content. With sensitivity labels and protection settings applied to more files sooner, organizations can better prepare their data estate for Microsoft 365 Copilot with greater confidence.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: An auto-labeling policy can apply a label that encrypts SharePoint or OneDrive content.
claims.quote: When the auto-labeling policy includes locations for SharePoint or OneDrive, the label must be configured for the Assign permissions now setting, and User access to content expires must be set to Never.

claims.claim: Label-applied encryption restricts readability to authorised users.
claims.quote: Can be decrypted only by users authorized by the label's encryption settings.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A policy can replace a lower-priority manually applied label when configured to do so.
claims.quote: All locations: Applicable for emails and for files in SharePoint and OneDrive. When you select this setting, an existing sensitivity label will always be overriden if the sensitivity label you chose for the policy has a higher priority.

claims.claim: A label-removal policy can remove a manually applied label.
claims.quote: an auto-labeling policy configured to automatically remove a label can remove the selected label, including when the label was manually applied, and leave the content unlabeled.

claims.where: Risk assessment; Governance guidance; controls[1].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Turning a policy from Ready to turn on to On requires Compliance Administrator or Compliance Data Administrator.
claims.quote: Turning a policy from Ready to turn on to On requires Compliance Administrator or Compliance Data Administrator. Without one of these roles, the Turn on policy button appears greyed out even after a successful simulation.

claims.claim: Service-side auto-labeling operates without user interaction.
claims.quote: Because the user doesn't interact with the labeling process, auto-labeling policies don't support recommended labeling

claims.claim: A policy must run at least one simulation before automatically applying or removing labels.
claims.quote: You can't automatically label documents and emails, or remove labels, until your policy has run at least one simulation.

claims.claim: Simulation is the only documented pre-enforcement checkpoint.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Purview auto-labeling policy simulation only checkpoint approval before enable policy'; opened apply-sensitivity-label-automatically, including prerequisites, simulation workflow and activation instructions; no separate approval checkpoint found.

claims.claim: The update introduces no new labeling conditions.
claims.quote: This update does not introduce new labeling conditions, data storage locations, or protection capabilities.

claims.claim: The update introduces no new data storage locations.
claims.quote: This update does not introduce new labeling conditions, data storage locations, or protection capabilities.

claims.claim: The update introduces no new protection capabilities.
claims.quote: This update does not introduce new labeling conditions, data storage locations, or protection capabilities.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Labels applying encryption through SharePoint or OneDrive auto-labeling policies require Assign permissions now.
claims.quote: When the auto-labeling policy includes locations for SharePoint or OneDrive, the label must be configured for the Assign permissions now setting

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: For those encrypted labels, User access to content expires must be Never.
claims.quote: User access to content expires must be set to Never.

claims.claim: Files cannot be auto-labeled while open.
claims.quote: Files can't be auto-labeled if they're part of an open session (the file is open).

claims.claim: PDFs are skipped unless PDF labeling is enabled for the tenant.
claims.quote: If PDF labeling isn't enabled, PDFs are skipped entirely: PDFs aren't evaluated or sent for labeling, and no label is applied.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Policy labeling-progress information refreshes every 48 hours.
claims.quote: This progress information updates every 48 hours, so you can expect to see the most current data about every other day.

claims.claim: The licensing model is included within qualifying existing auto-labeling licences.
claims.quote: | Service-side auto-labeling (SharePoint, OneDrive, Exchange) | Microsoft Purview portal → Information Protection → Policies → Auto-labeling policies | Same E5 / P2-tier SKUs as above |

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The listed qualifying SKUs are Microsoft 365 E5, E5 Compliance, E5 Information Protection & Governance and Azure Information Protection Premium P2 standalone.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 E5, Microsoft 365 E5 Compliance, Microsoft 365 E5 Information Protection & Governance, Azure Information Protection Premium P2 (standalone)

claims.claim: Learn lists the same E5/P2-tier SKUs for client-side and service-side auto-labeling.
claims.quote: | Service-side auto-labeling (SharePoint, OneDrive, Exchange) | Microsoft Purview portal → Information Protection → Policies → Auto-labeling policies | Same E5 / P2-tier SKUs as above |

claims.claim: Learn says auto-labeling of files and emails is not included with E3 or Business Premium.
claims.quote: You have E3 or Business Premium. Auto-labeling of files and emails isn't included at this SKU.

claims.claim: Learn says those customers require an E5/P2-tier add-on for auto-labeling.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labels and manual labeling are — auto-labeling requires an E5 / P2-tier add-on.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate charge, meter or licence specific to the higher ceiling is documented in the cited material.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Purview auto-labeling 500,000 higher daily limit additional charge meter license simulation checkpoint existing policies'; opened apply-sensitivity-label-automatically and searched its pricing/licensing text; also read roadmap 567890 and MC1461154. No ceiling-specific charge found.

claims.claim: Viewing file contents in simulation source view requires Data Classification Content Viewer.
claims.quote: To view file or email contents in the source view, you must have the Data Classification Content Viewer role

claims.claim: Global admins do not hold Data Classification Content Viewer by default.
claims.quote: Global admins don't have this role by default.

claims.claim: PDF and Word, Excel and PowerPoint files are supported.
claims.quote: PDF documents and Office files for Word (.docx), PowerPoint (.pptx), and Excel (.xlsx) are supported.

claims.claim: A detached OneDrive account not associated with its corresponding user account is unsupported.
claims.quote: A OneDrive account that isn't associated with its user account (sometimes called a detached OneDrive account) isn't supported for auto-labeling or simulation.

claims.claim: Sensitivity labels must be enabled for Office files in SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: To auto-label files in SharePoint and OneDrive: You have enabled sensitivity labels for Office files in SharePoint and OneDrive.

claims.claim: The maximum is 100 auto-labeling policies per tenant.
claims.quote: Maximum of 100 auto-labeling policies per tenant.

claims.claim: The Auto-labeling page is not visible where a backend Azure dependency makes the functionality unavailable.
claims.quote: Auto-labeling isn't currently available in all regions because of a backend Azure dependency. If your tenant can't support this functionality, the Auto-labeling page isn't visible in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The capacity increase is on by default for the active policies it targets.
claims.quote: The increased processing limit will automatically apply to existing active auto-labeling policies.

claims.claim: Nothing is documented about this capacity increase changing tenants with no auto-labeling policies.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Purview auto-labeling 500,000 files capacity increase no existing policies automatic configuration'; read MC1461154 and apply-sensitivity-label-automatically. No change for policy-free tenants was attributed to this capacity increase.

claims.claim: Simulation has a separate limit of 20,000,000 matched files per policy simulation.
claims.quote: Simulation mode supports up to 20,000,000 matched files. If more than this number of files are matched from an auto-labeling policy, you can't turn on the policy to apply the labels.

claims.claim: Policy locations can be edited through Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > Edit policy > Choose locations where you want to apply the label.
claims.quote: Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies. ... select the Edit policy button. ... Choose locations where you want to apply the label: Select and specify locations for Exchange, SharePoint, and OneDrive.

claims.claim: Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity <PolicyIdParameter> -AddSharePointLocation <SharePointSites> adds SharePoint locations to an existing policy.
claims.quote: Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity "Main PII" -AddSharePointLocation "https://my.url1","https://my.url2" -AddOneDriveLocation "https://my.url3","https://my.url4"

claims.claim: The corresponding parameter for adding OneDrive locations is -AddOneDriveLocation.
claims.quote: The AddOneDriveLocation parameter specifies the OneDrive sites to add to the list of included sites when you aren't using the value All for the OneDriveLocation parameter. You identify the site by its URL value.

claims.claim: Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy runs in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: The default All configuration is exempt from the portal's 1,000-explicit-SharePoint-site limit.
claims.quote: In the portal, each policy can target up to 1,000 explicitly included or excluded SharePoint sites ... If you keep the default configuration of All, this configuration is exempt from these maximums.

claims.claim: An eligible simulated policy can be enabled through Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > Turn on policy.
claims.quote: Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies. ... Select your policy to see the details ... When you're ready to run the policy without simulation, select the Turn on policy option.

claims.claim: Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity <PolicyIdParameter> -Mode Enable enables policy actions.
claims.quote: The Mode parameter specifies the action and notification level of the auto-labeling policy. ... Enable: The policy is enabled for actions and notifications.

claims.claim: -Mode TestWithoutNotifications selects the test mode.
claims.quote: TestWithoutNotifications: An audit mode where no actions are taken, and no notifications are sent (Test mode).

claims.claim: -Mode Disable switches the policy off.
claims.quote: Disable: The policy is disabled.

claims.claim: Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > View details opens per-policy review pages with Labeled items and Labeling failures.
claims.quote: go to Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies. Select a policy, then select View details in the policy details panel. ... The newer review page has separate Overview, Labeled items, and Labeling failures tabs.

claims.where: controls[2].api; controls[2].note; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Export-ActivityExplorerData -Filter1 @("Activity", "LabelApplied") exports matching labeling activity rather than configuring the ceiling or reproducing the per-policy review pages.
claims.quote: Use the Export-ActivityExplorerData cmdlet to export activities ... For example, @("Activity", "LabelApplied") returns records with the activity value LabelApplied.

claims.claim: Learn advises reviewing the failure reason even when few files fail.
claims.quote: Review the failure reason even when few files fail. Transient infrastructure failures are retried automatically, but file format, protection, or label configuration failures might require action regardless of volume.

claims.claim: In the Microsoft Purview portal, Audit > Start recording user and admin activity enables auditing.
claims.quote: Select the Audit solution card. ... Select the Start recording user and admin activity banner.

claims.claim: Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true turns on auditing in Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: Connect to Exchange Online PowerShell. ... Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true

claims.claim: Turning auditing on or off requires the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online to turn auditing on or off.

claims.claim: The start-recording banner appears when auditing is not already enabled.
claims.quote: If auditing isn't turned on for your organization, a banner is displayed prompting you to start recording user and admin activity.

claims.claim: Organisation auditing must be enabled for auto-labeling simulation.
claims.quote: Simulation mode: Auditing for Microsoft 365 must be turned on.

claims.claim: The Activity explorer export cmdlet runs in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: Using the Activity explorer export cmdlet requires assigned permissions.
claims.quote: To use this cmdlet in Security & Compliance PowerShell, you need to be assigned permissions.

claims.claim: Activity explorer reports on up to 30 days of data.
claims.quote: Activity explorer reports on up to 30 days worth of data.

claims.claim: None of the calls in the table sets the tenant-wide 500,000-file ceiling itself.
claims.quote: The AddSharePointLocation parameter specifies the SharePoint sites to add to the list of included sites ... The Mode parameter specifies the action and notification level of the auto-labeling policy.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist asks administrators to check policy conditions, but the controls table only documents location selection for policy scope.
claims.quote: confirm each one's SharePoint and OneDrive locations and conditions still match your intent. / Which SharePoint and OneDrive locations an auto-labeling policy covers
claims.fix: The first Before rollout checklist step's instruction to check policy conditions has no corresponding controls-table entry; the existing first row covers locations, not conditions.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist asks administrators to check label-encryption settings, but no controls-table row represents those settings.
claims.quote: Check every label used by a SharePoint or OneDrive policy: those that apply encryption need Assign permissions now and User access to content expires set to Never.
claims.fix: The third Before rollout checklist step, checking Assign permissions now and User access to content expires on sensitivity labels, has no corresponding controls-table entry.
